subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Electric current is defined as the rate of flow of:
questions.explain: Current I = charge / time, measured in amperes.

questions.q: If 60 C flows past a point in 20 s, the current is:
Potential difference is the energy transferred per unit:
questions.explain: V = energy/charge (volts = joules per coulomb).

questions.q: Ohm's law is:
questions.explain: For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, V is proportional to I.

questions.q: A resistor carries 2.0 A at 12 V. Its resistance is:
An ohmic conductor is one for which:
options: Current is proportional to voltage at constant temperature
questions.explain: Its V-I graph is a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: Two 4.0 ohm resistors in series give a total resistance of:
questions.explain: Series resistances add.

questions.q: Two 4.0 ohm resistors in parallel give a total resistance of:
questions.explain: Equal parallel resistors give R/2.

questions.q: In a series circuit the current is:
questions.explain: A single path means one value of current.

questions.q: Components in parallel share the same:
questions.explain: Parallel branches have equal voltage; current divides between them.

questions.q: Electrical power can be found from:
questions.explain: Also P = I^2 R = V^2/R.

questions.q: A device at 12 V drawing 2.0 A uses power:
A 3.0 ohm resistor carries 2.0 A. Power dissipated is:
The resistance of a wire depends on length, cross-sectional area and:
questions.explain: R = rho L / A.

questions.q: The emf of a cell is the:
options: Energy given to each unit of charge by the cell
questions.explain: emf is total energy per coulomb before internal losses.

questions.q: The terminal voltage of a real battery is less than its emf due to:
questions.explain: V = emf - Ir when current flows.

questions.q: Increasing the length of a uniform wire makes its resistance:
questions.explain: Resistance is proportional to length.

questions.q: A long, thin wire compared with a short, thick wire (same material) has:
questions.explain: Greater length and smaller area both raise resistance.

questions.q: Kirchhoff's current (junction) law expresses conservation of:
questions.explain: Current in equals current out at a junction.

questions.q: Kirchhoff's voltage (loop) law expresses conservation of:
questions.explain: Potential differences around a closed loop sum to zero.
